scientificBoundaries: The map, distance matrix, species and dispersal coefficients are fictional teaching assumptions, not measured Galapagos dispersal rates or a full ecological forecast.
With dispersal enabled, shorter routes have higher individual odds; when the captured migration scale is zero all route odds are zero.
Expected crossings are source N at G-1 multiplied by the selected-route probability, not a guarantee of integer arrivals. The source changes when a route is reversed.
Both outgoing routes and staying are mutually exclusive destinations from one dispersal draw and their probabilities sum to one.
Actual movement carries copies into the destination pool; realized newborn contribution is reconstructed from actual parent identities and independently sampled marker slots.
Transmitted copies can exceed arrivals, and an arrival may leave no copies in the newborn cohort. Copies are not distinct offspring counts.
The destination pool includes residents who stayed and migrants from both other islands. Parent origin refers to the previous generation rather than ultimate ancestry.
One neutral marker’s p and H=2p(1-p) do not measure genome-wide diversity; empty cohorts have undefined means, frequencies and H.
G0 has no recorded dispersal round or captured crossing odds. Future settings do not become historical G0 evidence.
A route observation alone does not establish coevolution or the causal effect of geography; the existing controlled repeated research study provides broader comparisons.
